scope: Actual single-key BINARY/NOCASE/RTRIM auxiliary indexes, including declared column collations and expression/partial programs: physical key ordering, NULL-aware uniqueness, native actions, consumed scalar collations, metadata and independently checked rollback/WAL files. Finite admitted cases, not global SQLite equivalence.

negative_results.reason: Non-BINARY key expressions and declared collations were rejected in SQL or independent opening.
Actual key comparators, uniqueness, replacement victims and metadata match.
Six declared-column full-index cases still used the ordinary BINARY-only model in each file mode.

Generic source parsing let leading-whitespace ordinary column declarations enter the auxiliary decoder. The original catalog-admission unit regression caught this; auxiliary decoding now requires an actual expression, predicate or non-BINARY key.

Native SQLite ignores unused inner unknown collations under lower/concatenation/CASE; min and comparison operations resolve collations they consume. The initial blanket validator was replaced, with all controls retained in the final 100-case driver.

implementation: Existing SQLite BINARY/NOCASE/RTRIM comparators sort real physical key values followed by actual rowids; NULL-aware unique checks and actual replacement-victim selection use the same selected comparator.

Prepared scalar programs annotate actual declared column collations in both key and partial predicate. Index comparison metadata comes from an outer COLLATE or direct column declaration, independently of inner scalar metadata.

Pure schema compilation resolves collations consumed by comparison/min/max/nullif/IN/CASE operations. Actual unknown selected collations report their native name; unused scalar metadata remains inert.

Declared non-BINARY simple column indexes enter the source-certified physical branch in live DDL and independent acquisition. Ordinary BINARY index admission/canonical certificates remain on their prior branch.

Direct and virtual metadata report actual column cid or expression cid=-2 and the actual key collation. The existing independent key decoder and rollback/WAL index codecs consume these actual key orders. The C VFS shim is unchanged.

evaluation_protocols.public_file_modes: 7528 complete stdout/exit/first-error and independent persisted catalog/row/integrity comparisons, including 100 collated-index cases with fresh generated values.
evaluation_protocols.same_connection: 254 actual API continuation cases: 167 retained general, 29 partial, 27 expression and 31 new collated-index cases, each suite reported separately.
evaluation_protocols.crashes: 420 finite SIGKILL timing samples, including 24 new collated-key samples; real production recovery followed by independent SQLite schema/row/index-key/cookie/integrity observations. No every-syscall, power-loss, arbitrary-schedule or global root identity claim.
evaluation_protocols.named_features: The original 88-probe survey still has four failures: WITHOUT ROWID and composite primary keys, each in both file modes. This finite survey is not a global coverage percentage.

proof_scope: All retained contracts and required audits compile. The newly audited uniqueConflict_null law applies to the live selected-collation uniqueness function; prior source-text, selected-row membership/truth and physical rowid laws remain. Independent checked-image contracts execute the actual collated-key validation. A new maintained Lean group checks selected collation/column identity, NOCASE IGNORE/REPLACE, physical metadata and declared-collation predicates. No global collated-index/SQL/planner equivalence theorem is claimed.
limitations: Four original named survey failures remain: WITHOUT ROWID and composite primary keys, both file modes.

Auxiliary index query-planner selection, composite keys, implicit collated UNIQUE/PRIMARY table constraints and auxiliary unique-index foreign-parent admission remain work. Recursive auxiliary REPLACE with DELETE programs, non-ABORT primary policies, ALTER, UPSERT, UTF-16 auxiliary index IO and broader scalar error/phase combinations remain work.
Bulk physical root-page layout is not globally SQLite-identical; pending new-object schema metadata and larger root-preservation cases remain separate work.
Wider error codes/phases, FAIL/IGNORE/ROLLBACK controls, triggered UPSERT, INSTEAD OF/temp triggers, writable CTEs, trigger-aware ALTER and deferred private-function declarations remain work.

UTF-16 writes/setters, native-key/materialization limits, pending new physical allocations and earlier SQL/storage limitations remain. The finite process-kill samples do not establish every syscall/power-loss schedule.
